request.text: write a 150 word story about a fox, delete-during check
request.reply:
Flick, a russet fox, padded silently through the golden underbrush of the autumn woods. His tail, a brush of burnt orange, twitched with caution as the air grew crisp and smelled of damp earth. He was hunting, the subtle shift in the wind carrying the scent of small, unsuspecting prey. 

Suddenly, a flash of movement caught his eye near the mossy creek bank. A plump field mouse darted across the fallen leaves. Flick lowered himself, his muscles coiled springs of grace and instinct. Just as he prepared to pounce, a loud, unexpected crack echoed through the woods—a branch snapping under a larger creature. 

The mouse froze. Flick hesitated, his hunter's focus momentarily broken. The forest held its breath. After a long silence, the mouse scurried deeper into its hole, and Flick, sensing the danger, melted back into the shadows, the hunt unfinished but the memory of the near-capture sharp.
